# sophosfirewall_application_filter_policy (Resource)

Manages an application filter policy (*Protect > Applications > Application filter*). Firewall rules apply a policy through `security_features.application_policy`. Rules are evaluated top to bottom, so their order matters. Each rule matches either a list of individual `applications` or applications selected by filters: `categories`, `risks`, `characteristics`, `technologies`, `classifications`, `smart_filters` and `other_filters`. Within a filter any value matches; the firewall lists valid values under *Protect > Applications* and GET /application/attributes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Rules are evaluated top to bottom. Each rule matches either individual
# applications or applications selected by filters.
resource "sophosfirewall_application_filter_policy" "office" {
  name        = "office-apps"
  description = "Allow collaboration tools, block evasive and high-risk apps"

  rules = [
    {
      name         = "allow-collaboration"
      action       = "allow"
      applications = ["Microsoft Teams", "Slack", "Zoom"]
    },
    {
      name            = "deny-evasion"
      action          = "deny"
      categories      = ["Proxy and Tunnel"]
      characteristics = ["Can bypass firewall policy", "Tunnels other apps"]
    },
    {
      name       = "deny-p2p-office-hours"
      action     = "deny"
      categories = ["P2P"]
      schedule   = "Work hours (5 Day week)"
    },
  ]
}

# Firewall rules apply the policy to allowed traffic.
resource "sophosfirewall_firewall_rule" "lan_to_wan" {
  name              = "lan-to-wan"
  action            = "accept"
  source_zones      = ["LAN"]
  destination_zones = ["WAN"]

  security_features = {
    application_policy = sophosfirewall_application_filter_policy.office.name
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name of the application filter policy. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `rules` (Attributes List) Ordered policy rules (at least one). Changes replace the whole rule set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the object assigned by the firewall.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `action` (String) Action for matching applications. One of `allow`, `deny`.
- `name` (String) Name of the rule, unique within the policy.

Optional:

- `applications` (Set of String) Individual applications to match by name, e.g. `Discord` or `Microsoft Teams` (see *Protect > Applications > Application list* or GET /application/apps). Conflicts with the filter attributes.
- `categories` (Set of String) Application categories to match, e.g. `P2P`, `Proxy and Tunnel` or `General Business`.
- `characteristics` (Set of String) Characteristics to match, e.g. `Can bypass firewall policy`, `Bandwidth Intensive` or `Widely Used`.
- `classifications` (Set of String) Cloud application classifications to match, e.g. `Sanctioned`. A classification filter only matches cloud applications: the firewall adds a `characteristics` filter with `Cloud Application` to the rule, which is not reported as drift when `characteristics` is not configured.
- `other_filters` (Map of Set of String) Additional filters keyed by API attribute name, for attributes the firewall supports beyond the ones above. Each value is the set of attribute values to match.
- `risks` (Set of String) Risk levels to match, as listed by the firewall for the `risk` attribute.
- `schedule` (String) Name of the schedule during which the rule applies. Defaults to `All The Time`.
- `smart_filters` (Set of String) Smart search expressions to match application names against, e.g. `live`.
- `technologies` (Set of String) Technologies to match, e.g. `Browser Based` or `Client Server`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by name or UUID.
terraform import sophosfirewall_application_filter_policy.example <name-or-uuid>
```
